name: LLM Evaluators
description: Test your knowledge of how large language models are measured and assessed.

questions.question: What is the primary goal of LLM evaluation?
options: To measure performance on given tasks
To increase the model's parameter count
To shorten the model's training time
questions.explain: Evaluation aims to quantify how well a model performs on targeted tasks so developers can compare and improve models.

questions.question: Which metric is commonly used to evaluate LLM-generated text fluency?
questions.explain: Perplexity measures how well a language model predicts the next token, reflecting the fluency of generated text.

questions.question: What does the acronym BLEU stand for in NLP evaluation?
questions.explain: BLEU stands for Bilingual Language Evaluation Understudy, a metric for comparing machine-translated text to reference translations.

questions.question: Which evaluation approach compares LLM outputs against human-generated references?
questions.explain: Reference-based evaluation measures output quality by comparing generated text to a set of human-written reference texts.

questions.question: What is task-specific evaluation in the context of LLMs?
options: Evaluating the model on a narrow task
questions.explain: Task-specific evaluation focuses on how well the LLM performs on one particular task such as summarization or question answering.

questions.question: Which evaluation metric estimates how well an LLM’s probability predictions align with the true distribution of tokens in a dataset?
questions.explain: Perplexity measures how well the model predicts token probabilities.

questions.question: What is a key limitation of using BLEU scores for LLM evaluation?
options: It requires GPU acceleration to run
It only works with code generation tasks
It misses paraphrases with equivalent meaning
It cannot be computed without human annotators
questions.explain: BLEU relies on exact n-gram matches to a reference, so it can penalize paraphrases that are semantically equivalent.

questions.question: Which method evaluates an LLM by prompting it to judge its own outputs?
questions.explain: LLM-as-a-judge is a method where a powerful model is used to score the outputs of another model, acting as an automated evaluator.

questions.question: What does hallucination refer to in LLM evaluation?
options: When the model states false facts confidently
When the model refuses to answer a valid prompt
When the model outputs code instead of prose
When the model responds more slowly than usual
questions.explain: Hallucination occurs when the model produces information that sounds confident but is factually wrong or fabricated.

questions.question: What evaluation metric quantifies the percentage of an LLM's factual statements that are supported by evidence from a trusted source?
questions.explain: It measures factual consistency against a trusted source.
